mcqs.question: Two vectors A and B have the same magnitude of 10 N. Vector A makes an angle of 30° with the positive x‑axis, while vector B makes an angle of 60° with the positive x‑axis. Which statement correctly compares their rectangular components?
mcqs.explanation: For vector A: A_x = 10 cos30° = 8.66 N, A_y = 10 sin30° = 5 N. For vector B: B_x = 10 cos60° = 5 N, B_y = 10 sin60° = 8.66 N. Hence A_x is larger than B_x while A_y is smaller than B_y, which matches option A. The other options either claim equality or reverse the inequalities, which are incorrect.

mcqs.question: A vector of magnitude 25 m is directed 40° above the positive x‑axis. What are its rectangular components (x‑component, y‑component)?
mcqs.explanation: x = 25 cos40° = 25 × 0.7660 ≈ 19.2 m; y = 25 sin40° = 25 × 0.6428 ≈ 16.1 m. Option A gives the correct pair. Options B, C and D either swap the components or use incorrect trigonometric values.

mcqs.question: A vector has components V_x = 6 m/s and V_y = 8 m/s. What is the magnitude of the vector?
mcqs.explanation: Magnitude = √(V_x² + V_y²) = √(6² + 8²) = √(36 + 64) = √100 = 10 m/s. Option A is correct; the other options result from incorrect arithmetic or forgetting to take the square root.

mcqs.learning_point: Use component methods in physical problems
mcqs.question: Why is the component method preferred when analyzing the motion of a projectile?

options.A: It allows independent treatment of horizontal and vertical motions.
options.B: It eliminates the effect of gravity.
options.C: It converts vector quantities into scalars.

mcqs.answer: It allows independent treatment of horizontal and vertical motions.
mcqs.explanation: Projectile motion can be split into horizontal (constant velocity) and vertical (uniformly accelerated) components, which can be solved separately and then combined. Gravity still acts vertically, so option B is false. Components remain vectors, not scalars, so C is false. The motion is still two‑dimensional overall, making D incorrect.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly defines the resolution of a vector into components and distinguishes it from scalar addition?

options.A: Resolution breaks a vector into perpendicular vector parts; scalar addition combines magnitudes without direction.
options.B: Resolution splits a vector into any two parts; scalar addition requires perpendicular directions.
options.C: Resolution yields scalar components; scalar addition yields vectors.
options.D: Resolution is only for forces; scalar addition is for velocities.

mcqs.answer: Resolution breaks a vector into perpendicular vector parts; scalar addition combines magnitudes without direction.
mcqs.explanation: Resolving a vector means expressing it as two (or three) mutually perpendicular vector components that retain direction. Scalar addition merely adds numbers, ignoring direction. Options B, C, and D contain inaccurate statements about the nature of resolution and scalar addition.

mcqs.question: A force of 50 N acts at 30° above the horizontal. What are its horizontal and vertical components?
mcqs.explanation: Horizontal component = 50 cos30° = 50 × 0.866 ≈ 43.3 N. Vertical component = 50 sin30° = 50 × 0.5 = 25 N. Option A matches these values. Options B swaps the components, while C and D use incorrect trigonometric values.

mcqs.question: A displacement vector has components 12 m east and 5 m north. What is its magnitude and direction measured north of east?
mcqs.explanation: Magnitude = √(12² + 5²) = √(144 + 25) = √169 = 13 m. Direction θ = tan⁻¹(5/12) ≈ 22.6° north of east. Option A gives both correctly. Option B uses the complementary angle, C has wrong magnitude, D assumes a 45° angle.

mcqs.learning_point: Use component methods in physical problems
mcqs.question: A ball is thrown with an initial speed of 20 m/s at 30° above the horizontal. Ignoring air resistance, what is the horizontal range of the ball?
mcqs.explanation: Horizontal component Vx = 20 cos30° = 17.32 m/s. Vertical component Vy = 20 sin30° = 10 m/s. Time of flight = 2Vy/g = 2×10/9.8 ≈ 2.04 s. Range = Vx × time = 17.32 × 2.04 ≈ 35.3 m, rounded to 35 m. Option A matches this result; the other options are off by several metres.
